steps: Title: One Term, 2026 era, Pakistan (three red dots, tough), Normal
Read the desk, All orders catalogue, searched orders
Queued then removed a nuclear strike on India to see the preview (53% success, 8% def)
Approved all staff suggestions and executed month 1 to 12
Tried to switch to Map mode at month 12 (screenshots hung)
scenarios.notes: I understood the order catalogue and costs, but never learned why individual orders are refused or what the hidden limits are. I played 11 months on staff autopilot, which kept me alive and tension falling; that is exactly the dominant-strategy smell.

steps: Pressed Approve staff suggestions and Execute every month
Mission bonus needs score 115 and relations -70 with Afghanistan
scenarios.notes: Approve-all appears to be a safe default move; I could not tell in 12 months whether any active play beats it, because nothing tells me what would.

friction.where: Desk, All orders: dimmed orders (Strike nuclear sites, Declare war, Sabotage)
friction.expected: A tooltip or line saying what is missing (target, capital, rule)
friction.happened: Clicking or hovering a dimmed order does nothing and shows no reason. Without a target the chips just sit there.

friction.where: Month debrief and top bar: Score
friction.expected: A line saying why score fell 3 while approval, stability and legitimacy rose
friction.happened: Score went 100 to 97 with every visible meter up. The table says only 'War weariness weighs on the public mood'. Score kept sliding to 93 with no breakdown.
Month 2 crisis re-used the month 1 refugees rally image.
The same Afghan leader call with 'Offer talks on a ceasefire' as the staff suggestion at months 5, 7, 8 with nearly identical text.
The click-by-label failed on the tab and on several buttons whose labels contain extra text (needed to tap text or coordinates).

friction.expected: Enter on a half-typed query to do nothing risky
friction.happened: Enter on 'nuclear strike india' instantly queued a nuclear site strike with no confirm. I removed it, but an accidental Enter would have queued it.

friction.expected: Parity with the desk and a normal screenshot
friction.happened: After switching to Map at month 12, every screenshot timed out for minutes (machine load was high, so unconfirmed). I could not test map and desk parity.

friction.expected: To see the capital refill rule
friction.happened: Showed 1 left of 3 almost every month; I never saw how capital is earned or why it stays low.

bugs.title: Dimmed orders give no reason
steps: Click or hover 'Strike nuclear sites in ...' without a target

bugs.title: Enter in order search queues a nuclear strike with no confirmation
bugs.expected: Selection or confirmation for an irreversible order
bugs.actual: Strike on India queued at once

bugs.title: Crisis card art repeated from previous crisis

suggestions.what: Show the reason on every dimmed or refused order, in the chip itself, with the rule and what unlocks it
A score breakdown (four 50-point components, target vs current, monthly delta) one tap from the top bar
A 'what if I do nothing but approve all' baseline so I can see whether active play beats autopilot, and make staff picks sometimes wrong
Make staff suggestions vary and react to the state; stop repeating the same call

delight: Table view of the month debrief with a 'Why your numbers moved' row and before/after numbers (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/dan-term/018-table.png)
Order search with typed targets and previews (53% success, defence cost) (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/dan-term/015-nukeIndia.png)
Crisis options show signed effect arrows and who backs each option (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/dan-term/006-desk1.png)
Globe title screen and newspaper look crafted (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/dan-term/001-title.png, devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/dan-term/024-p5e.png)

fun.reason: Good setup and crises, but 11 of 12 months on approve-all with little to decide.

clarity.reason: Debrief table is great; score movement and capital rules are opaque.

visual.reason: Illustrated crisis scenes, newspaper and globe look crafted, apart from repeated art.

feels_like_a_game.reason: Feels designed, not a dashboard, though the staff autopilot makes it feel like a managed menu.

agency.reason: Dimmed orders silently refuse; I never knew the rule behind them.

realism.reason: Pakistan's dilemmas (Afghan war, Iran refugees, India) are right, but Afghan calls repeat.

replay.reason: Unproven; I could not find whether anything beats autopilot in 12 months.

recommend.reason: I would tell Paradox friends to wait until score is explained and autopilot is not enough.

quit_point: Month 8: the Afghan ceasefire call came back with the same text, score still sliding, and I had decided nothing beyond Approve all for seven months. I would have stopped that evening.
verbatim: Show me why the score moved and why an order is refused, and make approve-all not good enough, and then it is a game.
